The searches did return a controlled trial from April 2026 that the entry does not hold (the treatment entries, the claims, the self-experiments and the publications log were searched for the trial's name, its first author and the journal). Stanfield, Leroux, Kaeberlein and colleagues reported in the Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle (online 2026-04-15) a trial in which 40 inactive adults aged 65 to 85 followed a home exercise programme for 13 weeks and took either 6 milligrams of rapamycin once a week or a placebo. On the main measure, how many times a person can stand up from a chair in 30 seconds, the rapamycin group gained about two fewer repetitions than the placebo group, a difference that was not statistically significant; in the secondary analyses of those who completed the trial the difference did favour placebo. It is a controlled result at an ageing dose in older people, and it goes against the test, not for it. Also returned, in search results only: a rapamycin dosing trial in San Antonio, Texas, said to have a safety review due in October 2026, with no report of that review found.
